jobs.title: Senior Program Manager - Payment Operations - Healthcare
jobs.description:
Job Description

Our Opportunity

Chewy's mission is to be the most trusted and convenient destination for pet parents and partners everywhere. We view pets and pet parents as family and are obsessed with meeting their needs and exceeding expectations through every interaction. Within Chewy, the Payments team improves the customer and care team experience by launching better ways to pay, increasing payment success, strengthening reliability, and reducing the cost and friction of payments.

Chewy is hiring a Senior Program Manager, Payment Operations - Healthcare
in Bellevue, WA, Plantation, FL, or Boston, MA
to lead payment health, readiness, and optimization across Chewy Healthcare. In this role, you will be the senior operational owner for in-clinic, digital, and recurring payments used by customers and clinic care teams, and internal operators. You will manage performance, partner escalations, and cross-functional execution for capabilities that are critical to customer experience and business outcomes.

The ideal candidate is an experienced payments and operations leader who has owned outcomes in a scaled retail, fintech, ecommerce, marketplace, subscription, or omnichannel environment. This person combines payments depth with senior program leadership and can move between strategic planning and hands-on issue resolution. They have improved one-time and recurring payment experiences, including authorization performance, stored credentials, tokenization, retry strategies, and decline recovery. They can quickly build credibility, simplify complex topics, identify customer and business impact, and lead partners across Product, Engineering, Clinic Operations, Customer Care, Analytics, Finance, Accounting, Legal/Compliance, and external payment providers.

What You'll Do

Own the operational roadmap for Healthcare payments across in-clinic, digital, and recurring workflows.
Define, monitor, and improve payment metrics such as success rate, authorization performance, recurring payment recovery, terminal reliability, refund/void quality, decline trends, incident volume, and SLAs.
Strengthen recurring payment operations, including stored credential health, tokenization, card lifecycle events, payment retries, decline recovery, account updater processes, and payment method reliability.
Lead Healthcare payment launches, enhancements, defect resolution, and operational readiness across Product, Engineering, Clinic Operations, Customer Care, Analytics, Finance, Accounting, Legal/Compliance, and external partners.
Identify payment defects and reliability risks, quantify customer and financial impact, and drive prioritized resolution.
Build and improve operating mechanisms such as dashboards, runbooks, escalation paths, incident response processes, post-incident reviews, partner reviews, and readiness checklists.
Manage external payment providers, terminal providers, gateways, processors, and other third parties against SLAs, roadmap dependencies, issue resolution, and improvement plans.
Lead incident response and root-cause analysis in partnership with internal and external teams; convert learnings into durable prevention and monitoring mechanisms.
Develop executive-ready narratives, business reviews, and recommendations that connect payment performance with customer experience, care team experience, cost, risk, and business impact.
Serve as a payments subject matter expert for card-present, card-not-present, recurring payments, terminal, refund, reconciliation, and operational support workflows across Healthcare.

What You'll Need

Bachelor's degree in business, finance, operations, technology, or related field, or equivalent practical experience.
8+ years of experience in payments, payment operations, fintech, ecommerce, retail, healthcare operations, marketplace operations, subscription/recurring payments, or another scaled operational environment.
5+ years leading complex cross-functional programs with Product, Engineering, Analytics, Finance, Accounting, Customer Care/Operations, Legal/Compliance, and external partners.
Track record owning payment KPIs and operational outcomes such as payment success rate, authorization rate, decline rate, terminal availability, refund/void performance, dispute rate, reconciliation quality, cost of payments, or SLA performance.
Direct experience with card-present and card-not-present payment flows, including gateways, processors, acquirers, issuers, card networks, digital wallets, payment terminals, stored credentials, tokenization, settlement, refunds, disputes, and reconciliation.
Experience with recurring or subscription-like payment programs, including stored credentials, payment retries, decline recovery, account updater/card lifecycle management, payment method lifecycle events, or recurring billing reliability.
Experience supporting omnichannel, healthcare, clinic, field, retail, marketplace, ecommerce, or service-oriented environments where both customer and operator workflows matter.
Strong analytical capability with the ability to use payment data, processor reporting, decline trends, defects, and customer/care team feedback to identify root causes and drive action.
Proven ability to operate in ambiguity, dive into details, and lead issue resolution without direct authority.
Strong vendor and partner management experience, including performance reviews, escalations, SLA management, roadmap alignment, and operational improvement plans.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing executive-level narratives, business reviews, and decision recommendations.
Ability to deliver time-sensitive initiatives while maintaining strong attention to detail and follow-through.
Ability to travel up to 15% of the time.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with payment terminals, order management, point-of-sale systems, ecommerce, or healthcare/clinic payment workflows.
Experience launching or scaling payment capabilities across physical locations, field operations, or distributed teams.
Experience improving payment observability, incident response, support models, or partner performance in a high-volume environment.
Experience with digital wallets, debit routing, account updater/card lifecycle management, or payment optimization strategies.

Success in This Role Looks Like

Healthcare payment workflows are reliable, measurable, and supported by clear operating mechanisms across in-clinic, digital, and recurring experiences.
Customer, clinic, and care team friction is identified quickly, quantified clearly, and resolved through strong cross-functional ownership.
Payment partners are managed through business reviews, escalations, SLAs, and improvement plans.
Payment incidents have clear response paths, root-cause ownership, durable prevention actions, and improved monitoring.
Senior leaders have a clear view of payment performance, risks, tradeoffs, and investment needs across Chewy Healthcare.

The base salary range for this role is $118,500 - $207,000.00.

The specific salary offered to a candidate may be influenced by a variety of factors including but not limited to the candidate’s relevant experience, education, and work location. In addition, this position is eligible for 401k and a new hire and annual equity grant. C08+ positions may also be eligible for annual bonus.

We offer different types of insurance and benefits, such as medical/Rx, vision, dental, life, disability, hospital indemnity, critical illness, and accident. We offer parental leave, family services benefits, backup dependent care, flexible spending accounts, telemedicine, pet adoption reimbursement, employee assistance program, and many discounts including 10% off pet insurance and 20% off at Chewy.com.

Exempt salary team members have unlimited PTO, subject to manager approval. Team members will receive six paid holidays per year. Team members may be eligible for paid sick and family leave in compliance with applicable state and local regulations.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, gender, citizenship, marital status, religion, age, disability, gender identity, results of genetic testing, veteran status, as well as any other legally-protected characteristic. Title: Case Manager – Pathways to Recovery

Posting Date: July 20, 2026

Location: Integrity House - Morris Plains

Are you searching for a fulfilling place to develop your career and make an impact? Join Integrity House, New Jersey’s oldest active nonprofit provider of compassionate care for individuals and families experiencing addiction and mental health conditions. We’ve been a trusted source in our field since our founding in 1968, and our goal has remained constant: to provide our clients with comprehensive, whole-person care options under one unified system of care. Integrity House operates 16 licensed treatment programs across New Jersey as well as community outreach and prevention programs, and serves over 3,000 individuals every year.

We are excited to announce our Case Manager
opening in Morris Plains, NJ and Secaucus, NJ. The Case Manager is responsible for coordinating participant enrollment, assessments, Individual Employment Plans (IEPs), supportive services, workforce development coordination, and employment retention services for the Pathways to Recovery program. The Case Manager serves as the primary point of contact for participants and collaborates with employers, One-Stop Career Centers, training providers, and community partners to remove barriers to employment and promote long-term success.

Key Responsibilities

Participant Engagement, Assessment & Service Planning

Recruit, screen, and enroll eligible participants through community outreach, referrals, workforce agencies, treatment providers, criminal justice agencies, healthcare organizations, and other community partners.
Conduct participant orientation, explaining program expectations, participant rights and responsibilities, available services, confidentiality, attendance requirements, and employment expectations.
Complete comprehensive participant assessments to evaluate employment history, educational background, vocational interests, work readiness, strengths, barriers, supportive service needs, and career goals.
Coordinate required assessments including workforce readiness evaluations, literacy assessments, vocational interest inventories, and other assessment tools utilized by the program.
Develop Individual Employment Plans (IEPs) that establish measurable employment, education, training, and supportive service goals.
Review and revise IEPs regularly based upon participant progress, changing needs, and employment outcomes.
Maintain regular participant contact to encourage engagement, accountability, and successful completion of program objectives.

Case Management & Supportive Services

Maintain an assigned caseload and provide ongoing individualized case management services throughout participant enrollment.
Conduct regularly scheduled case management sessions to assess progress, identify barriers, and develop appropriate intervention strategies.
Coordinate supportive services necessary to reduce barriers to employment including transportation, childcare, work clothing, identification documents, housing referrals, legal assistance, work supplies, and emergency resources.
Coordinate referrals to behavioral health providers, substance use treatment programs, healthcare providers, educational institutions, financial assistance programs, and community-based organizations.
Utilize motivational interviewing, trauma-informed care, and strengths-based interventions to encourage participant engagement and promote self-sufficiency.
Monitor participant participation in scheduled services and address attendance concerns through individualized intervention planning.
Maintain collaborative communication with internal staff and external providers to ensure continuity of care and coordinated service delivery.

Workforce Development & Employment Coordination

Coordinate participant enrollment into workforce readiness programming, occupational training, educational services, and career development activities.
Collaborate with the Workforce Readiness Instructor, GED Instructor, and Employment Specialist to monitor participant progress and ensure successful completion of assigned activities.
Assist participants in identifying career pathways consistent with their interests, skills, abilities, and long-term employment goals.
Prepare participants for employment through career planning, interview preparation, workplace readiness reinforcement, and coordination of occupational training opportunities.
Monitor participant completion of certifications, credentials, and training requirements necessary for employment.
Coordinate participant referrals for interviews, job placement opportunities, internships, and work-based learning experiences.
Conduct employment retention follow-up, identify workplace concerns, and coordinate interventions to promote long-term employment success.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Social Work, Human Services, Psychology, Sociology, Counseling, Criminal Justice, Public Health, Workforce Development, Education, or a related field required.
Master’s Degree preferred.
Minimum two (2) years of experience providing case management, behavioral health services, workforce development services, vocational rehabilitation, recovery support, or other human services.
Experience working with individuals impacted by substance use disorders preferred.
Experience working with justice-involved populations preferred.
Demonstrated knowledge of community resources and workforce systems.
Strong organizational and leadership abilities.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Required Licensing or Certifications

Valid New Jersey Driver’s License.
CPR/First Aid certification preferred.
CADC, CPRS, CHW, or other human services credential preferred but not required.

Schedule:

This is a full-time position. The employee is generally expected to work Monday through Friday during normal business hours. However, flexibility is required to accommodate participant schedules, employer meetings, recruitment events, community outreach activities, workforce readiness cohorts, and other program operations. Occasional evening and weekend hours may be required. The Case Manager is expected to travel throughout the designated service region to conduct participant meetings, attend employer visits, participate in community partnership meetings, collaborate with One-Stop Career Centers, coordinate supportive services, and participate in recruitment and outreach activities.

Overview

Our Commitment to Equity

The Y actively promotes a culture free from bias and injustice. We are dedicated to removing institutional and systemic barriers that result in oppression and racism. We will be accountable to marginalized communities for creating equitable and sustainable environments where social justice is woven into every facet of our programs, and by caring for our communities in a culturally versatile and respectful manner.

Job Summary

This position will be instrumental in further developing the Foundational Community Supports (FCS) program. This position will assist program leadership to train, lead and expand the Foundational Community Supports program at the Y Social Impact Center. Supports low-income youth and young adults who may have experience in foster care, homelessness, disconnection from school, juvenile justice and/or other systems in developing the skills to live independently. Provides program coordination, operational support and leads staff trainings for the FCS Program. Assists program directors in advancing program and operational goals. Provides program participants with a welcoming and supportive environment.

This position is at the Social Impact Center Y, the social services branch of YMCA of Greater Seattle (YGS). The mission of the Social Impact Center Y is to accelerate young people’s ability to build safe, successful, and happy lives. Every year, we serve 5,000 children, youth, young adults, and families across King County with programs that aim to strengthen young people’s ability to develop to their fullest potential through four strategies: reducing risk factors; navigating systems towards successful life transition; ensuring stability, safety and wellness in times of crisis; and building competencies and social capital. The Social Impact Center Y’s programs include housing, behavioral health, foster care licensing, violence prevention, education, and employment. Many of the young people we serve have had involvement in the foster care, criminal justice system, and/or homelessness systems.

What you'll get from working at The Y

Membership to the YMCA of Greater Seattle for you and your household
Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life insurance
Retirement with generous employer contributions
Free access to mental health resources

Teaches life skills, job readiness or other subject matter individually and/or in groups, often experientially. Teams effectively and collaboratively with YMCA staff and/or community partners to plan and facilitate activities, including visits to related resources in the community. May coordinate delivery of life skills workshops.
Builds and maintains collaborative relationships with funding liaisons, other service providers, businesses and/or educational institutions as related to specialized services.
Supports participant success in key domains such as safe and stable housing, permanent connections to supportive adults, education and employment, health and well-being, and life skills.
Assists with accurately completing monthly billing and reporting.
Participates in on-call rotation for FC Permanency.

All employees and volunteers are responsible for adhering to abuse prevention policies, maintaining appropriate boundaries, completing required training, reporting suspicious or inappropriate behavior, and complying with mandated reporting requirements.

Responsible for ensuring staff are properly screened, trained, supervised and held accountable to the organization’s abuse risk management standards.

CORE JOB SUMMARY

Moreover, this employee provides a broader oversight to daily program activities in support of the University’s mission. The Senior Clinical Program Coordinator evaluates the financial performance of programs to meet departmental goals and assist in the development of short- and long-range budgetary planning.

Core Job Functions

Supervises, directs, and coordinates assignments for the given program. Trains, develops, and empowers staff to effectively perform their jobs. Evaluates program effectiveness, analyzes results, and recommends appropriate action. Coordinates program activities with other program, department or staff activities, ensuring optimum efficiency. Acts as a main point of contact for project funders, advisors, speakers, and participants, and recruits program participants, members, and volunteers. Oversees various personnel actions, including but not limited to, hiring, performance appraisals, disciplinary actions, termination, employee time records, and other related activities. Develops cooperative relationships with patients and families by projecting a positive image and creating a professional atmosphere. Develops program communications and promotional literature for distribution, including newsletters, brochures, and flyers. Prepares and presents periodic reports, financial statements, and records for management or outside agencies. Makes suggestions to leadership including the process changes that will improve overall performance. Maintains required records and reports statistics for administrative, quality assurance, and safety and control purposes. Maintains patient confidentiality as well as the confidentiality of hospital business information. Oversees the maintenance of established supply levels in unit and supply rooms. Adheres to University and unit-level policies and procedures and safeguards University assets.

This list of duties and responsibilities is not intended to be all-inclusive and may be expanded to include other duties or responsibilities as necessary.

Qualifications

CORE QUALIFICATIONS

Education:

Bachelor’s degree in relevant field

Experience:

Minimum 3 Years Of Relevant Experience

Knowledge, Skills and Attitudes:

Ability to communicate effectively in both oral and written form.
Ability to handle difficult and stressful situations with professional composure.
Ability to maintain effective interpersonal relationships.
Ability to understand and follow instructions.

DEPARTMENT ADDENDUM

Department Specific Functions

Assist Clinical Program Manager as assigned.
Assist Manager with development of best practices for departmental sub-specialties.
Assist with establishing procedures to ensure reproducibility of each sub-specialty service.
Meet with outside vendors as requested/needed when manager is not available.
Assist in training employees on the importance/performance of tasks.
Assist manager to create/run reports for review of sub-specialty service performance.
Provides support to the clinical operation for their assigned sub-specialty sections by liaising between pathologists, clinical areas (internal/external), customer care, histology, and ancillary laboratories.
Assist with expediting or facilitating clinical sample requests by coordinating with histology lab, sub-specialty, or customer care teams.
Obtaining and examining all relevant information to assess validity of complaints from patients, clinical staff, and physicians to determine possible causes, and identify solutions.
Contacting clinical staff/faculty on behalf of sub-specialty in response to inquiries.
Reviewing assigned service line pending lists (UM & JMH) and conferring with pathology attendings and trainees regarding delays and escalations.
Processing of pathologist-initiated send out orders (e.g. NGS) and monitoring of send out portals to integrate results into EMR (UCHART), and LIS (CoPath).
Preparing sub-specialty TB and associated documents in a timely fashion as well as approving or denying add-on requests by clinical teams.
Processing in-house (add-on) testing requests made by clinicians.
Overseeing of all client & personal consult cases for completeness, material return, and resulting.
Review of sub-specialty add-on testing approval & QA forms for completeness.
Processing of private and client autopsies; documentation and release of results (may depend on specialty).
Maintains Research/Educational Databases (may depend on specialty).
Identify cases for Research Projects (may depend on specialty).
Protects sensitive patient medical records through the strict following of the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) protocols.
Completion of all additional duties & projects, as assigned by manager, in a timely fashion.

The University of Miami offers competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, tuition remission and more.

UHealth-University of Miami Health System, South Florida's only university-based health system, provides leading-edge patient care powered by the ground breaking research and medical education at the Miller School of Medicine. As an academic medical center, we are proud to serve South Florida, Latin America and the Caribbean. Our tradition of excellence has earned worldwide recognition for outstanding teaching, research and patient care. We're the challenge you've been looking for.

jobs.description:
Description

If another position becomes available within five months of this recruitment’s closing date, the applicant pool from this posting may be used to fill additional vacancies.

When you come to work for New Jersey Judiciary you will join an 8500-member strong TEAM that operates with the highest standards of independence, integrity, fairness and quality service. You will be engaged with work that has purpose, meaning and makes a difference in lives of the public we serve. We work hard every day to build the public’s trust and confidence in our court system, which includes issues such as bail reform, marijuana decriminalization and recovery court. Whether it be in a courtroom, an administrative office, a courthouse training room, an IT office or in the field, our Judiciary workforce is improving the lives of countless individuals and families every day. We honor the dignity and individualism of each member of our organization while fostering professionalism and continuous improvement in our work.

SALARY:
The salary range for this position is $61,749.69 to $$100,154.67 for Schedule A, and $61,749.69 to $95,146.95 for Schedule B. For newly hired individuals, the starting salary will normally be at the minimum of the salary range. For current Judiciary employees, salary upon promotion or advancement will be an increase of 5% of base salary, not to exceed the maximum of the range, or the minimum salary of the band/level, whichever is greater.Judiciary employees hired prior to June 3, 2014, are considered Schedule A. Newly hired individuals, and Judiciary employees hired on or after June 3, 2014, are considered Schedule B.

The Judiciary offers a strong opportunity for growth.

The New Jersey Judiciary is seeking a goal-oriented self-starter with excellent written and oral communication skills who is committed to providing exceptional customer service and has strong technical capabilities to work as an Administrative Specialist 3 in the Civil Practice Division. Under the direction of a Court Executive 2B (Chief, Civil Court Programs), the selected individual will act as coordinator for the Civil Practice Division in the complementary dispute resolution (CDR) area.

REMOTE WORK
:
The Judiciary currently offers a hybrid work schedule, and this position may qualify for up to 2 days of remote work outside of Judiciary buildings. To participate in this program, in addition to installing a multifactor authentication app on your phone or tablet, you will be required to have high speed home internet access.

Example of Duties

Regular and predictable physical presence at the worksite is an essential function of this position.

The Selected Individual’s Responsibilities Will Include

Overseeing the Civil Mediation and Arbitrator Access Databases to review, approve or reject new mediator applications, remove mediators and arbitrators who have not completed ongoing training requirements, and advise vicinage managers, supervisors, and staff on issues related to mediators and arbitrators
Preparing and analyzing statistical reports
Coordinating and presenting at arbitrator trainings
Developing and implementing policies and procedures
Providing quality customer service, including communicating Court Rules and Judiciary policies and procedures to mediators, attorneys, judges, litigants, vicinage staff, organizations and the public
The selected individual will also coordinate and serve as a trainer for new and existing Civil education programs and perform other duties as assigned to accommodate the Civil Practice Division’s workload and organizational needs.
Maintain the rosters of Special Civil Part Officers (SCPOs) and facilitating credentialing (e.g. badges) for SCPOS.

NOTE: Civil Practice experience, including complementary dispute resolution, and experience in conducting trainings is preferred for this position.

Qualifications

Graduation from an accredited college or university with a bachelor's degree and three years of professional experience, one of which shall be in program development, program coordination, program analysis, program administration and/or administrative research.

Substitution:
Applicants who do not possess the required education may substitute additional paraprofessional and/or professional experience on a year-for-year basis with one year of such experience being equal to 30 semester hour credits. An associate degree from an accredited college or university and two years of additional paraprofessional and/or professional experience may be substituted for a bachelor’s degree.

A master’s degree from an accredited college or university may be substituted for one year of experience.

A law degree from an approved American Bar Association law school may be substituted for two years of experience.

Note: A master’s degree or a law degree from an accredited college or university, may be used as a substitution, not both.

Education Note:
Degrees conferred outside of the United States must be evaluated by a recognized evaluation service. (See https://naces.org/members/ )

Supplemental Information

Driver's License:
Appointees will be required to possess a driver's license valid in New Jersey only if the operation of a vehicle is necessary to perform essential duties of the position.

Authorization to Work:
US citizenship is not required. Selected candidate must be authorized to work in the US according to Department of Homeland Security, US Citizenship and Immigration Services regulations.

Special Note:
Newly hired employees must agree to a thorough background check that will include fingerprinting. All data received will be kept in strict confidence except to inform the individual of the findings and what action will be taken as a result of this information.

Residency Law:
In accordance with N.J.S.A. 52:14-7 (L. 2011, Chapter 70), the "New Jersey First Act," all persons newly hired by the Judiciary within one year must establish, and then maintain, principal residence in the State of New Jersey. Any person may request an exemption from that requirement from the Employee Residency Review Committee in the Department of Labor & Workforce Development on the basis of either hardship or employer critical need.

How To Apply

The NJ Judiciary requires all applicants to complete the application process fully and as instructed. All applicants must complete the work experience and education sections and attach any required documents. Applications must describe all relevant work experience in detail, beginning with your current or most recent job, including military service (indicate rank), internships and job-related volunteer work, if applicable. Use a separate section to describe each position. Applicants who indicate "see resume" or enter their initials to acknowledge that they have skipped the Work History and Education sections will not be considered, unless they do not possess any education history or work experience. Only applicants that follow the application instructions and submit completed applications will be considered.

The New Jersey Judiciary consists of: the Supreme Court, the Superior Court including the Appellate Division and the Trial Court of the 15 vicinages in New Jersey, the Tax Court and the Municipal Court System. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides technical assistance, operational support, training, research and development, budget and personnel coordination, and development and operation of information systems for the Courts of New Jersey.

The Judiciary of New Jersey is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action

jobs.description:
About Us

Augusta University is Georgia's innovation center for education and health care, training the next generation of innovators, leaders, and healthcare providers in classrooms and clinics on four campuses in Augusta and locations across the state. More than 12,000 students choose Augusta for educational opportunities at the center of Georgia's cybersecurity hub and experiential learning that blends arts and application, humanities, and the health sciences. Augusta is home to Georgia's only public academic health center, where groundbreaking research is creating a healthier, more prosperous Georgia, and world-class clinicians are bringing the medicine of tomorrow to patient care today. Our mission and values https://www.augusta.edu/about/mission.php make Augusta University an institution like no other.

Augusta University's distinct characteristics in education and research include real-world experiences and community engagement, as well as a culture of building community, corporate and government partnerships that address health, security, economic and societal concerns locally and across the state.

The University System of Georgia https://www.usg.edu/hr/orientation/welcome_to_the_board_of_regents_university_system_office is comprised of our 26 institutions of higher education and learning as well as the System Office. Our USG Statement of Core Values are Integrity, Excellence, Accountability, and Respect. These values serve as the foundation for all that we do as an organization, and each USG community member is responsible for demonstrating and upholding these standards. More details on the USG Statement of Core Values and Code of Conduct are available in USG Board Policy 8.2.18.1.2 and can be found online at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section8/C224/#p8.2.18_personnel_conduct.

Additionally, USG supports Freedom of Expression as stated in Board Policy 6.5 Freedom of Expression and Academic Freedom found online at https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section6/C2653 .

Location

Augusta University -

Our Health Sciences Campus: 1120 15th Street, Augusta, GA 30912

Our Summerville Campus: 2500 Walton Way, Augusta, GA 30904

College/Department Information

Established in the summer of 2002, the Center for Biotechnology and Genomic Medicine (CBGM) at the Medical College of Georgia (MCG) at Augusta University (AU) was developed to promote interdisciplinary and translational research in Biotechnology and Genomic Medicine with the ultimate goal of promoting predictive, preventive, personalized and participatory (4P) medicine. The Center's research efforts focus on two main areas: Discovery and validation of biomarkers for disease prediction and diagnosis; Pharmacomics and drug discovery for personalized medicine. CBGM is home of four internationally renowned programs in diabetes research: The Environmental Determinants of Diabetes in the Young, the Prospective Assessment in Newborns of Diabetes Autoimmunity, the Diabetic Complications Consortium, and the Mouse Metabolic Phenotype Consortium. Additional research programs include autoimmune diseases, transplantation, and cancer. These research programs are supported by an annual extramural funding of approximately $12 million. The center houses several state-of-the-art high throughput and high content facilities for genetics, genomics, proteomics, drug screening and bioinformatics.

Job Summary

Performs basic molecular and/or cellular biology techniques. Duties also include: support ongoing research projects, help develop and evaluate new research techniques and procedures, maintain a detailed and organized notebook with procedures and data, help maintain mouse lines, and make orders for the lab.

Responsibilities

The duties include but are not limited to:

EXPERIMENTS: Perform a variety of examinations of specimens for the presence of diseases and pathological conditions. Prepare culture media. Incubate and culture bacteria. Stain slides and perform molecular biology techniques.

EQUIPMENT: Calibrate and operate laboratory equipment such as spectrophotometer, microscope, coulter counter, centrifuge, hematic stainer, etc. Make orders for lab.

MOUSE COLONY: Maintain mouse lines and colonies.

OTHER: Perform other duties as assigned

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in chemistry, biology, biochemistry, cell biology, social sciences, natural sciences, life, health care, or materials science directly related to the research area to which the position is assigned and experience in a research or clinical setting.

OR

Associate's degree from an accredited college or university in chemistry, biology, biochemistry, cell biology, social sciences, natural sciences, life, health care, or materials science directly related to the research area to which the position is assigned and a minimum of three years' experience in a research or clinical area.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

KNOWLEDGE

Proficient in Microsoft Office and other computer software/databases.

Skills

Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.

Detail-oriented with strong prioritization and organizational skills.

Abilities

Ability to maintain confidentiality.

Shift/Salary/Benefits

Shift: Days; M-F (Work outside of the standard business hours may be required)

Pay Band: B5

Salary: $17.88/hourly - $21.63/hourly

Salary to be commensurate with qualifications of the selected candidate within the established range (generally minimum-midpoint) of the position

This position is (fully/partially) funded through external sources. Continued employment is contingent upon the availability of these funds.

Recruitment Period: Until Filled

Augusta University offers a variety of benefits to full-time benefits-eligible employees and some of our half-time (or more) employees.

Benefits that may be elected could include health insurance, dental insurance, life insurance, Teachers Retirement System (or Optional Retirement Plan), as well as earned vacation time, sick leave, and 13 paid holidays.

Also, our full-time employees who have been employed with us successfully for more than 6 months can be considered for the Tuition Assistance Program. Consider applying with us today!

Conditions of Employment

All selected candidates are required to successfully pass a Background Check review prior to starting with Augusta University.

If applicable for the specific position based on the duties: the candidate will also need to have a credit check completed for Positions of Trust and or approved departmental Purchase Card usage.

Motor vehicle reports are required for positions that are required to drive an Augusta University vehicle.

For Faculty Hires: Final candidates will be required to provide proof of completed academic degree(s) as well as post-secondary coursework in the form of original transcript(s). Those candidates trained by a foreign institution will also be required to provide an educational/credential evaluation.

All employees are responsible for ensuring the confidentiality, availability, and integrity of sensitive [patient, student, employee, financial, business, etc.] information by exercising sound judgment and adhering to cybersecurity and privacy policies during their employment and beyond.

Other Information

This position is also responsible for promoting a customer-friendly environment and providing superior service to our patients, students, faculty, and employees. "Augusta University is a patient-and family-centered care institution, where employees partner every day with patients and families for success."

Augusta University is a tobacco-free environment, and the use of any tobacco products on any part of the campus, both inside and outside, is strictly prohibited.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Augusta University is proud to be an equal opportunity employer welcoming applicants from underrepresented groups, including individuals with disabilities and veterans.

Consider applying with us today!

Description

The Street Heath Outreach Program is an innovative project which identifies homelessness, chronic health, and mental health needs in Central Alameda County. The program will assist people in attaining housing stability and improve health and well-being.

Using a multi-disciplined team approach, the program provides street and venue-based outreach and engagement, assessment, health services and triage, case management, as well as linkages to housing agencies and mental health services. The program will work with all participants to develop and carry out action plans that improve health and wellness.

Under the supervision of the Director of Population Health, the Street Health Outreach Community Health Worker
will work directly with participants to access housing programs, assist with enrollment and/or maintenance of Medi-Cal or HealthPAC, and provide navigational support to successfully engage participants to a medical home. Other activities include health education, care plan development, public benefit linkage and assisting the participant with accessing TVHC health care services.

Schedule:
This is a full-time position, working 40 hours per week, typically Monday through Friday, with occasional Saturday hours.

About TVHC:
Tiburcio Vasquez Health Center is a nonprofit community health center dedicated to promoting the health and well-being of our community by providing accessible, high-quality care through the integration of primary care, dental care, WIC support, mental health counseling, community health education, and more.

Benefits:
We offer excellent benefits, including: medical (100% paid co-payments, premiums, etc.), dental, vision (including dependent and domestic partner coverage), generous paid leave benefits including holidays, Flexible Spending Accounts, retirement plans with an Employer match, tuition reimbursement, monthly treats, pet insurance, and more.

*As position is grant-funded, employment is subject to the availability of grant funding*

Compensation
: $24.00 - $26.00 per hour, depending on experience.

This position is represented by SEIU, with compensation and benefits determined by the terms of the Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA). Salary is based on the wage scales outlined in the agreement. Beyond base pay, TVHC provides a comprehensive compensation package that supports the health, wealth, and career development of our employees.

Responsibilities

Engages, empowers and advocates for Alameda County unsheltered residents and helps them achieve their best health.
Conducts regular street outreach and engagement, building trust with individuals encountered at encampments and other service locations according to the responsive schedule.
Attends to immediate survival needs as prioritized by clients, e.g. distributing basic necessities and supplies.
Provides problem-solving support using Motivational Interviewing techniques.
Creates a care plan that reflects the client’s need based on outreach assessment.
Coordinates linkages to various community resources to meet these needs and works from an interdisciplinary approach.
Provides case management services in a culturally, linguistically and age appropriate manner.
Serves as a liaison between the client, community and health and social services.
Assists clients with enrollment and maintenance of MediCal and Medicare eligibility as well as with other benefits such as CalFresh, GA and SSI.
Provides culturally competent, trauma informed health services.
Maintains client information and case documentation in a confidential and professional manner.
Completes Coordinated Enrry Assessments for individuals seeking housing.
Maintains client data and responsible for updating county database on a monthly basis.
Adheres to organizational policy and procedures.
Builds and maintains appropriate relationships with staff, encampment leaders and Housing Resource Centers.
Supports a positive work environment and fosters teamwork.
Represents Street Outreach team at county and community based organization events and meetings.
Participates with other staff in multidisciplinary meetings and other staff processes to achieve program development, staff development, program evaluation, program operations review, and other activities as appropriate.

Requirements

High school diploma, or equivalent required.
Associate of Arts Degree preferred.
Valid Cardio Pulmonary Resuscitation Card (CPR) within three months of hire.
Minimum of one (1) year experience providing outreach to chronically unhoused individuals preferred.
Experience with Electronic Medical Records (EHR) preferred.
Lived experience of homelessness valued.

Qualifications

Bilingual; English/Spanish preferred.
Be highly dependable and independent.
Good communication; ability to work well within a team and independently.
Proficiency in computer operations, navigational skills and comfortable with Internet-based applications.
Sound decision-making skills including problem solving.
Professional demeanor.
Sensitivity to and understanding of the special needs of unsheltered people facing complex challenges.
Excellent communication, organizational and time management skills with the ability to meet tight timeframes.
Strong understanding of the health care and community resources.
Must be willing to travel to assigned locations and drive street health medicine van to and from various service sites as needed.
Ability to work effectively and collaboratively.
Flexible and adaptable to change.
Ability to learn quickly and retain complex information.
Ability to travel to work assignments.

The Community Services Department is seeking a dedicated, detail-oriented, and service-driven professional to serve as the Community Services Coordinator for the RC Community Center. This position oversees the daily operations of the facility, including youth and family services, community programming, facility rentals, and specialized onsite amenities. A primary responsibility is the strategic management and promotion of the facility rental program to maximize community use and generate revenue alongside classes and other programming opportunities. The Coordinator also provides leadership to a team of part-time staff, fostering a collaborative, safe, and customer-focused environment while creating meaningful experiences that strengthen connections and enhance the quality of life for Rancho Cucamonga residents.

When you join Team RC, you are joining a progressive, collaborative organization that values innovation, equity, and continuous professional growth. We take pride in our world-class facilities, diverse recreational offerings, and a workplace culture rooted in teamwork, respect, and a shared passion for public service. If you are looking for a meaningful career where your daily work directly impacts families, shapes local culture, and leaves a lasting legacy, this is where you belong.

The Community Services Department is responsible for providing enriching, fun, and meaningful opportunities for the community to come together. The department operates the Epicenter Sports Complex, RC Community Center, RC Sports Center, Victoria Gardens Cultural Center, Goldy S. Lewis Community Center, and James L. Brulte Senior Center. In addition to the listed facilities above, more than 30 different parks are open to the community for passive use.

The Community Services Department’s guiding principles are the core values by which we operate and are central to how we get things done: Integrity, Humility, Teamwork, Curiosity, Inclusivity, and Zeal. Programming, Rentals & Contract Classes

Preparing and compiling reports regarding program participation, attendance, revenues, and expenses.
Managing and maintaining accurate files, data, and contractual agreements, including MOUs, instructor/vendor agreements, and community partnerships, to ensure compliance and positive relationships.
Utilizing ActiveNet facility booking software to seamlessly manage classes, camps, workshops, events, and facility allocations.

An ideal candidate will be a highly organized, energetic, and proactive professional who thrives in a fast-paced community center environment. This individual will possess a unique blend of business acumen and people-first leadership, with a proven track record of supervising, training, and mentoring part-time staff to deliver exceptional customer service. The ideal candidate is a strategic problem solver who can seamlessly shift from administrative duties—such as managing operating budgets, optimizing rental revenue, and drafting vendor MOUs—to hands-on facility logistics, including routine facility operations. Responsibilities:
• Manage a caseload of 60-90 units, supporting formerly homeless individuals with diverse needs, including mental health challenges, substance use, and medical concerns.
• Conduct outreach visits upon tenant entry, provide ongoing assessments, and deliver tailored case management services focused on housing retention and quality-of-life improvements.
• Assist tenants in maintaining housing by fostering relationships, addressing challenges, and implementing effective intervention strategies.
• Support tenants in accessing and managing benefits, including rent payments, while addressing unit habitability concerns and participating in regular inspections.
• Refer tenants to employment programs, community services, and other resources, ensuring successful follow-through and connection.
• Organize and lead tenant-focused events and activities to foster a supportive community environment.
• Respond to tenant crises with de-escalation strategies and provide necessary interventions.
• Maintain accurate case files and records, ensuring confidentiality and compliance with organizational standards.
• Collaborate with internal teams and external service providers to advocate for tenant needs and deliver comprehensive support.
• Participate in agency-wide initiatives, including annual recertification processes, and support administrative tasks such as check disbursement days.
• Bachelor’s degree or at least 2 years of verifiable experience providing case management services to homeless or formerly homeless individuals.
• Minimum of 1 year experience working with diverse, low-income, or homeless populations.
• Proven expertise in case management and outreach, with knowledge of San Francisco resources for homeless individuals.
• Ability to manage organized case files for a caseload of 60-90 tenants.

new_jobs.title: Career Pathways Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Ridgeline is hiring for a full-time Career Pathways Program Manager. Note: this listing has been updated as of July 22, 2026 to reflect the full-time nature of this role.

About Ridgeline

Ridgeline is a Bay Area nonprofit education-to-employment intermediary. We connect young people ages 16–22 from underserved communities to high-wage careers, backwards mapped from employer demand. This Career Pathways Program Manager role is focused on healthcare and maritime, two of the region's highest-demand sectors, both offering strong wages and clear career ladders with or without a four-year degree.

We are the connective infrastructure between education and industry – building the pathway together so that what young people do in the classroom, at a clinical site, and on the waterfront adds up to a coherent path to a career. Our programs are organized into three phases.

In Explore (Grades 11-12)
, students enter through short-form career intensives and multi-month paid cohort programs, designed to build career clarity, durable skills, and professional networks.
In Build (Grades 12-13)
, young people complete paid work-based learning placements with employer partners, earn industry-recognized credentials, and gain early college credit.
In Launch (post-secondary)
, young people step into employment, apprenticeship, or degree programs anchored by those same employers.

Every program is paid and at every phase, the goal is the same: a high-ROI next step for the young person. Demand for our programs has consistently outpaced capacity by 3x. We are hiring our first dedicated program team, scaling what's working and piloting what's next.

About the Career Pathways Program Manager Role

We are seeking a full-time Career Pathways Program Manager
to partner with the Co-Founder and Head of Program as the primary program design, operations, and facilitation lead. This role is equal parts designer, organizer, and facilitator
: you will translate big-picture ideas into dynamic career-connected learning experiences while also ensuring smooth operations and serving as a consistent, trusted adult presence for youth participants.

Because Ridgeline is an intermediary – coordinating across multiple school, employer, and college partners simultaneously rather than sitting inside any single institution – this role requires someone who thrives in multi-stakeholder environments as much as in the room with young people.

Responsibilities:

Includes but are not limited to:

Program Design & Facilitation

Co-design pilot programming with the Head of Program, with emphasis on career exploration, durable skills, work-based learning, and social capital building
.
Develop activities and challenges that align with industry trends and program goals while centering participant voice and engagement.
Facilitate interactive sessions that blend hands-on learning, durable skill practice (e.g., communication, collaboration, AI fluency)
, and career exploration.
Build genuine relationships with participants — showing up as a consistent adult presence who encourages reflection, fosters community, and ensures every student is actively engaged.
Provide direct 1:1 support to enrolled participants, including e.g. coaching, career preparation support, and problem-solving as needs arise.

Operations & Coordination

Support student recruitment across partner schools and community organizations, and manage the application and selection processes
to build cohorts that reflect the communities Ridgeline serves.
Support program logistics
for pilots, including scheduling, communications, materials, and day-of execution.
Track program timelines and ensure details run smoothly so that program design and facilitation can shine.
Track and analyze participant outcomes
within and across programs; maintain shared data systems and contribute to regular progress reports.

Partnership & External Relationships

Co-design authentic, industry-informed learning sessions with experts.
Support guest speakers, mentors, and industry reviewers to deepen the real-world impact of programs.

Qualifications

Experience

3+ years designing and facilitating project-based, experiential, or career-connected learning
programs for young adults, especially in diverse or underserved communities.
Strong track record of program operations and coordination (e.g., scheduling, logistics, communication).
Demonstrated ability to balance big-picture program design
with detail-oriented execution
.

Skills

Exceptional facilitation and communication skills, with the ability to inspire, connect with, and support young adults (ages 16–22).
Highly organized and proactive project manager; comfortable juggling multiple moving pieces and stakeholders.
Strong collaborator and communicator who builds trust and alignment across teams, schools, and industry partners.
Creative problem-solver who adapts in real time to challenges while keeping program goals at the center.

Knowledge

Familiarity with healthcare and/or maritime/blue economy sectors is a plus.
Familiarity with CTE, dual enrollment, and work-based learning structures in California is a plus.
Clear understanding of durable skills
and how to embed them into learning experiences.
Awareness of systemic barriers to education-to-career pathways and a commitment to equity in design and facilitation.

Preferred Qualifications

Educators, facilitators, or instructional designers with experience in project-based or experiential learning
.
Nonprofit program managers with expertise in career readiness or workforce development
.
Coaches or trainers with background in apprenticeship, internship, or early-career pathways – bonus if you have direct experience working with young people (ages 16-22).

Role Details & Compensation

Salary:
The hiring range for this role is $92,000-$113,000. We use a consistent compensation framework across all roles. We will give our best offer and will not negotiate.
Benefits:
We are proud to offer a competitive benefits package including:
Health, Vision, and Dental
: Ridgeline covers 100% of your premium for medical, dental, and vision on our sponsored plan. We cover 75% for dependents. If you elect a high deductible medical plan, we contribute to your HSA to help you cover out-of-pockets costs. ‍

Retirement
: We match your 401(k) contributions dollar for dollar up to 5% of your salary. That match is fully vested from day one. ‍

Time Away
: Ridgeline hires exceptional people and treats them like it. We don't track vacation days or set a cap on time away because we don't think that's how great work happens.We trust you to make smart decisions about when to be present and when to step away. ‍

Sick and Wellness Time
: Ridgeline provides up to 10 days (80 hours) of paid sick time per fiscal year. ‍

Holidays
: Ridgeline observes all federal holidays plus two full company breaks: the last week of the calendar year and the first week of July. These are protected weeks to rest and recharge.
‍ Classification & Schedule:
This is a full-time, exempt position. This role can expect to work standard working hours Monday through Friday with out-of-school time (evening, weekend, holiday) work as needed to deliver programming. ‍

Location:
San Francisco Bay Area (Hybrid). Ridgeline operates on a hybrid schedule with Wednesday as a common in-person day. Staff are also expected to be present in person for student-facing programming, partner meetings, and team meetings as needed.

Application Process

Application Window:
We are collecting and reviewing applications on a rolling basis so applicants are encouraged to apply as soon as possible. To submit the online application you will need to login to a Google account
.

new_jobs.title: Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
The Program Manager leads Old Skool Cafe's youth development program. The Program
The manager is responsible for ensuring youth move successfully through program levels, meet
benchmarks, and receive high-quality coaching while contributing meaningfully to a high-stakes
hospitality environment.

The Program Manager operates as the organizational integrator across coaching, restaurant
operations, and community partnerships, balancing youth crises, restaurant service demands,
staff supervision, and partner communication in real time.

The youth development program has real foundations: passionate staff, established practices,
and institutional knowledge built over time. But those pieces have not been fully implemented
or unified into a coherent, metric-driven system. This role is being hired to build that
infrastructure: layering what exists into what can still be built, and driving the implementation
needed to make it operational.

This position provides the leadership, coordination, and operational discipline that keep the
youth development program aligned, accountable, and moving forward. The Program Manager
is responsible for ensuring that commitments become actions, plans become outcomes, and that
no youth or staff member falls through the cracks of organizational complexity.

Key Responsibilities

1. Cross-Departmental Coordination & Accountability
● Serve as the central point of contact across coaching, restaurant operations, and external
partnerships, ensuring clean handoffs between departments.
● Track commitments and deadlines across the coaching team, GM, Chef, and Director of
Communications, driving them to resolution or escalating as needed.
● Review cross-departmental priorities and unresolved issues during weekly leadership
meetings, driving decisions to resolution or escalating barriers as needed.
● Track youth enrollment, program readiness, and capacity indicators, and bring
data-backed analysis and recommendations to the Head of Operations on cohort size,
intake timing, and program capacity.

2. Coaching Supervision & Program Quality
● Provide direct supervision to the coaching team, including responsibility for staff
development, workload management, coaching quality, benchmark progress,
documentation, performance accountability, and maintaining a healthy, productive work
environment.
● Hold weekly one-on-one supervision meetings with each coach to provide feedback,
remove barriers, align priorities, support professional development, and address
performance concerns promptly, escalating unresolved issues in accordance with OSC
personnel policies.
● Support coaches by removing operational obstacles and providing professional
development, recognizing that coaches do their best work when they are supported,
developed, and held to clear expectations.
● Build upon the program structures, practices, and institutional knowledge already in
place, while developing and implementing the systems, benchmarks, and progression
frameworks still needed - layering what exists into what can still be built.
● Develop and implement a program roadmap for each level, building on existing practices
to create clear, defined, metric-oriented progression across all program levels.
● Implement and maintain the OSC Playbook workbook across youth, coaches, and staff,
establishing sustainable documentation systems and accountability practices that endure
despite individual staff turnover.
● Lead quarterly Individual Plans of Success (IPS) reviews with youth and adult teams.
● Identify systemic coaching gaps, including inconsistent documentation, benchmark
tracking, coaching practices, or youth engagement, and implement corrective actions.
● Lead implementation of new program processes and operational improvements, guiding
staff through change while maintaining consistency in youth experience and
organizational standards.

3. Youth Development & Restaurant Integration
● Organize and oversee the quality of youth recruitment interviews and screening
conducted with coaching staff, ensuring consistent eligibility standards across the team.
● Monitor youth progress across key milestones, addressing gaps and holding staff
accountable in follow-through directly with youth and staff.
● Partner with GM and Chef to integrate youth workforce training into daily restaurant
operations.
● Maintain an active presence during restaurant service to observe, coach, and reinforce
workplace behaviors, helping youth and staff translate life skills into real-time hospitality
practice.
● May carry a small direct caseload as capacity allows, using experience as a firsthand
source for identifying systemic gaps in coaching quality, documentation, or program
design.

4. Crisis Response & Staff Training
● Develop, plan, and facilitate ongoing staff development in Trauma-Informed Care,
Motivational Interviewing, Restorative Communication, Mandated Reporting, and
related topics based on program needs and emerging trends.
● Lead incident response for youth crises, disclosures, or safety concerns, and identify
early indicators of youth safety or wellbeing risk to intervene proactively rather than only
responding after disclosure.
● Serve as mandated reporter; ensure staff understand reporting obligations.
● Make referrals and facilitate connections to therapists and community support.
● Coordinate with probation officers, foster care workers, and mental health providers as
needed.
● Maintain strict confidentiality in accordance with policies and applicable laws.

5. Partnerships & Community Resources
● Develop, strengthen, and steward relationships with education, workforce development,
life skills, and community partners that expand opportunities for youth.
● Ensure externship placements support youth development and meet host organization
expectations.
● Cultivate existing partnerships and proactively develop new community relationships
that support youth development, workforce opportunities, and organizational impact.
Success Metrics
● 100% of youth receive weekly coaching, with documented outreach and follow-up for
missed engagements.
● OSC Playbook used consistently by youth, coaches, and staff; quarterly IPS reviews
completed on time.
● Life Coaches demonstrate ≥95% adherence to coaching and documentation standards.
● Partners consistently refer candidates and report positive program outcomes.
● Program data is accurate, current, and readily available for reporting and continuous
improvement.
● Program and operational gaps are identified within two weeks of discovery and either
resolved or escalated with documented action plans.

Qualifications

● Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Education, Nonprofit Management, or related field; or
8+ years relevant experience with at-risk youth.
● Demonstrated success leading complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives requiring
coordination across multiple teams.
● Demonstrated experience supervising, coaching, and developing professional staff while
fostering accountability and continuous improvement.
● Experience designing, improving, or implementing organizational systems, workflows, or
program processes in a dynamic environment.
● Comfortable navigating between existing structure and open space — able to build upon
what's already in place without dismissing it, while developing the systems and
frameworks still needed to make the program fully operational.
● Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret program data, identify trends, and
drive operational improvements.
● Demonstrated ability to influence outcomes and drive accountability without relying
solely on formal authority.
● Independent, self-directed problem solver who builds systems and structure without
needing to be handed direction, exercising sound judgment even when doing so requires
making difficult or unpopular decisions.
● Valid CA Driver's License; pass background check aligned with youth safety policies.
● Emotional maturity, empathy, and strong professional boundaries.
● Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to facilitate difficult
conversations and build trust across diverse populations.

Compensation & Benefits

OSC’s compensation program is designed to deliver Total Direct Compensation (based on role, level, and experience) that is at or above market. The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

Here, you'll work on technical design support assignments and provide solutions, learning continuously through ongoing training and on-the-job experience.

You will provide research support to develop accurate, robust, and precise assays. Your challenge will be to create value for Agilent through innovative ideas that either create new businesses or enhance existing ones. You will work in a cross-functional team dedicated to the design and development of CDx assays in a highly regulated environment and perform the following activities:

Supporting Stability Research Associates in the planning, execution, and documentation of stability studies for Companion Diagnostic (CDx) assays and assays in feasibility.

Recording experimental observations, collecting data, and communicating study progress, issues, and observations to the assigned Study Responsible and broader team.
Supporting multiple studies simultaneously while maintaining organization, accuracy, and attention to detail.
Following established procedures, protocols, and work instructions while recognizing and escalating discrepancies, unexpected results, or quality concerns.
Assisting with laboratory organization, inventory management, and other operational tasks that support study execution.
Collaborating with Stability team members and cross-functional partners to support project deliverables and timelines.
Contributing to continuous improvement efforts, including updates to templates, workflows, documentation tools, and knowledge repositories.
Participating in project team meetings to provide study updates and communicate laboratory observations.
May assist with data analysis, preparation of study summaries, protocol development, report generation, or presentation materials under the guidance of a Research Associate/Study Responsible.
Maintaining technical knowledge through training, scientific literature review, and participation in team learning activities.

requiring at least 3 on-site days per week, with additional on-site days as needed based on company needs.

BS/BA or MA in Biology, Biochemistry or related field
Ability to follow Quality System regulations including Design Control
Experience with immunohistochemistry and microscopy
Demonstrated problem-solving skills
Detail-oriented and organizational skills
Analytical skills and creativity
Proficient with Microsoft Office
Demonstration of excellent verbal and written communication
Ability to work both independently and within a team setting

Preferred Qualifications:

Background in biology techniques including immunohistochemistry, in situ hybridization, fluorescent techniques, protein biochemistry; cell biology and molecular biology
Background in one or more of the following: tumor biology, immunology, and histology
Experience with assay/protocol development

Job Description

Join the HJF Team!

HJF is seeking two highly organized, proactive, and detail-oriented Program Coordinators
to perform a wide range of administrative and operational research duties in support of the National Institute for Defense Health Cooperation (NIDHC). Specifically, this position will support the Pre-and Post-Crash Care (PPCC) Program, executed on behalf of the Department of Transportation's National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.

The Program Coordinator will serve as a central point of coordination for operational activities between internal and external stakeholders. The successful candidate will facilitate high-level communication and coordination across partner organizations, federal agencies, and internal HJF/USU leadership to ensure mission alignment. By managing complex scheduling, tracking key deliverables, and streamlining workflows, the Program Coordinator provides the essential administrative infrastructure necessary for the PPCC Team to effectively execute the program objectives.

The National Institute for Defense Health Cooperation (NIDHC) was established in 2025 by combining three defense entities: the National Center for Disaster Medicine and Public Health (NCDMPH), the Center for Global Health Engagement (CGHE), and the Defense Institute for Medical Operations (DIMO). Its mission is to support military and civilian health operational readiness in crisis and conflict through training and education, planning and partnership, and research and analysis. Based at the Uniformed Services University, NIDHC is a federal organization and academic center that supports the DoD and the federal interagencies.

The Henry M. Jackson Foundation for the Advancement of Military Medicine (HJF) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing military medicine. We serve military, medical, academic and government clients by administering, managing and supporting preeminent scientific programs that benefit members of the armed forces and civilians alike. Since its founding in 1983, HJF has served as a vital link between the military medical community and its federal and private partners. HJF's support and administrative capabilities allow military medical researchers and clinicians to maintain their scientific focus and accomplish their research goals.

Responsibilities

Provides administrative support under the direction of a supervisor, including assistance with hiring, purchasing, and tracking progress.
Supports in coordinating internal and external events and meetings, including venue procurement, planning coordination, materials support, and calendar management.

Supports in scheduling of meetings with stakeholders and project teams.

Coordinates documentation for Internal Review Board (IRB) submission.
Supports logistics for site visits, program reviews, and multi-agency meetings, including travel arrangements and facility coordination.
Performs other duties and responsibilities as assigned or directed by the supervisor.

Required Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to draft clear, professional documents.

Prior experience or strong foundational knowledge in EMS/emergency medical care, hospital systems, 911 dispatch operations, law enforcement, judicial systems, or operational research is highly desired.

new_jobs.title: RHTP Program Manager, Chronic Disease and Community Health Worker Integration
new_jobs.description:
RHTP Program Manager, Chronic Disease and Community Health Worker Integration

Position Description

Basic Job Purpose:
The Michigan Center for Rural Health (MCRH), Michigan's State Office of Rural Health, is seeking a highly motivated and skilled professional to serve as the Rural Health Transformation Program Manager for Chronic Disease and Community Health Worker (CHWs) Integration. This role requires a strong blend of experience in chronic disease program implementation, CHW workforce development, technical assistance delivery, and project management. This is not a direct clinical or patient care role. It is an opportunity to shape chronic disease programming and CHW integration at a statewide level, supporting rural health clinics and community-based organizations in improving care for patients living with hypertension, diabetes, and related conditions. The Program Manager will lead a portfolio of initiatives focused on CHW training and integration, chronic disease technical assistance, cross-sector care coordination, and learning collaborative facilitation across participating Rural Health Clinics (RHCs) under the Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Program. The Manager will serve as a trusted technical assistance provider and subject matter resource to rural sites and will help ensure measurable progress in chronic disease outcomes, CHW sustainability, and community-based care delivery.

Supervision Received:
Reports directly to the Director of Provider Solutions.

Typical Physical Demands

•       Prolonged periods of sitting.
•       Ability to hear and communicate within a normal range.
•       Ability to prepare reports and operate computer and phone equipment.

Typical Working Conditions

•       Hybrid Schedule: One in-office day per week, as a minimum (flexibility considered for exceptional candidates).
•       Travel to Rural Health Clinics across Michigan is expected, particularly for on-site technical assistance.

Performance Expectations and Core Competencies

•        Passion for Rural Health:
Demonstrates deep commitment to improving chronic disease outcomes and CHW integration in rural communities, continually working toward and often exceeding workplan goals.
•        Professional Communication and Relationship Building:
Engages with rural health clinic staff, CHWs, state partners, and community stakeholders with professionalism, respect, and clarity.
•        Collaboration and Teamwork:
Works cooperatively within MCRH and across external partners to advance shared rural health goals.
•        Excels at Customer Service:
Treats all people with utmost respect and responsiveness, strengthening relationships and advancing workplans and the MCRH Mission.
•        Personal Drive:
Has a passion to meet and exceed objectives in a thoughtful and time-driven manner.
•        Commitment to MCRH:
Aligns one's own behavior, leadership, and commitment with the needs, priorities, goals, and culture of MCRH.
•        Embraces Inclusion:
Creates an atmosphere that respects and embraces engagement of all people, ideas, and backgrounds.
•        Loves to Learn:
Able and willing to learn new skills and knowledge and accept new challenges to improve projects.
•        Manages Multiple Projects and Tasks:
Effectively manages time and resources to respond to needs while continuing to deliver on organizational goals, objectives, and timelines; and seeks help when needed in juggling priorities.
•        Systems-Level Project Management:
Effectively leads multiple statewide initiatives, balancing priorities, meeting deadlines, ensuring follow-through, and proactively seeking support when needed.
•        Personifies Teamwork:
Demonstrates good collaboration and communication to be effective in any team setting.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities

•       Lead the development, implementation, and ongoing improvement of site-specific technical assistance workplans for participating Rural Health Clinics, aligned with Rural Health Transformation Program priorities in chronic disease, CHW integration, and cross-sector care coordination.
•       Facilitate learning collaboratives, training sessions, and peer learning opportunities focused on chronic disease management, Community Health Worker integration, and care team development.
•       Provide individualized, on-site and remote technical assistance to rural health clinics implementing self-measured blood pressure programs, diabetes prevention and management initiatives, and multidisciplinary team-based care models.
•       Support CHW recruitment, onboarding, training alignment, and integration into rural care teams and workflows, including guidance on Medicaid billing readiness and CHW sustainability planning.
•       Conduct baseline assessments and ongoing evaluation activities across participating sites, including tracking performance indicators related to chronic disease outcomes, CHW activity, and cross-sector partnerships.
•       Develop and maintain a resource library of toolkits, workflows, case studies, and implementation guides in collaboration with subject matter experts and program partners.
•       Prepare required programmatic and fiscal reports and contribute to EGrAMS submissions in alignment with Michigan Department of Health and Human Services reporting requirements.
•       Represent rural CHW and chronic disease priorities within statewide and regional partner meetings, coalitions, and learning networks.
•       Contribute to MCRH grant writing efforts and identification of pilot opportunities to expand and sustain program impact.

Qualifications and Requirements

Knowledge and Skills

•       Strong understanding of chronic disease prevention and management, particularly hypertension and diabetes, and the role of Community Health Workers in rural care delivery.
•       Demonstrated project management experience, including the ability to work independently, manage multiple deadlines, and drive initiatives to completion.
•       Experience delivering technical assistance, training, or program support at the organizational or system level.
•       Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite; strong skills in data tracking, reporting, and documentation.
•       Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.
•       Ability to cultivate collaboration, build trust with rural partners, and facilitate cross-sector engagement.
